initiatives.name: Three-Year Transformation Programme
initiatives.summary: Schroders launched an ambitious multi-year transformation programme in Spring 2025 to simplify the business, improve cost efficiency, and return to sustainable profitable growth. The programme targets £150 million of annualised net cost efficiencies by the end of 2027, and is running ahead of schedule.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £150 million annualised net cost efficiencies target; £75 million in-year savings delivered (£102 million annualised)

evidence.title: Three-Year Transformation Programme Targeting £150m Savings
evidence.summary: Schroders launched an ambitious multi-year transformation programme in Spring 2025 to simplify the business, improve cost efficiency, and return to sustainable profitable growth. The programme targets £150 million of annualised net cost efficiencies by the end of 2027, and is running ahead of schedule.
evidence.quote: In financial terms our transformation is ahead of target, having already delivered £75 million of planned three-year net savings.

evidence.title: Transformation and Portfolio Restructuring Costs of £140.2m
evidence.summary: The Group recognized significant operating profit impacts from transformation costs (£79.4 million) and portfolio restructuring (£60.8 million), reflecting the scale of organizational change, including the gain on the SPW share exchange.
evidence.quote: The Group reported an impact on Operating profit for transformation costs of £79.4 million and portfolio restructuring of £60.8 million, including a gain on the share exchange for their 49.9% holding in Schroders Personal Wealth of £113.3 million.

evidence.title: Three-Year Growth Strategy: Simplify, Scale, Deliver
evidence.summary: In March 2025, Schroders launched a three-year strategic plan built around Simplify, Scale, and Deliver objectives, with specific financial targets across Public Markets, Schroders Capital, and Wealth Management to return the business to profitable growth.
evidence.quote: In 2025, we launched our three-year plan to return the business to profitable growth... Our strategic objectives enable us to focus and deliver long-term benefits for clients, shareholders and society. Simplify Scale Deliver

initiatives.name: Schroders Capital Growth Initiative
initiatives.summary: The Group committed up to £500 million of seed and co-investment capital to support the growth of Schroders Capital, funding new fund launches and strengthening client alignment, including deployments to the Greencoat Global Fund and BlueOrchard Climate Action Mobilisation Fund.

evidence.title: Schroders Capital Business Development Team Scaled to 40
evidence.summary: Schroders established and scaled a dedicated Schroders Capital Business Development team to reach a target of 40 sales specialists, enhancing client engagement and supporting private markets fundraising.
evidence.quote: Reached our target size of 40 professionals in the Schroders Capital Business Development team

evidence.title: Up to £500m Seed and Co-Investment Commitment to Schroders Capital
evidence.summary: The Group committed up to £500 million of seed and co-investment capital to support the growth of Schroders Capital, funding new fund launches and strengthening client alignment, including deployments to the Greencoat Global Fund and BlueOrchard Climate Action Mobilisation Fund.
evidence.quote: The Group has committed up to £500 million of seed and co-investment to support the growth of Schroders Capital.

initiatives.name: Cazenove Capital & Schroders Personal Wealth Restructuring
initiatives.summary: Schroders restructured its Wealth Management business by regaining full ownership of Cazenove Capital in exchange for its stake in Schroders Personal Wealth (SPW), a joint venture with Lloyds Banking Group. This was paired with new multi-year asset management agreements to manage SPW and Scottish Widows assets.
initiatives.investmentSummary: Gain on disposal of £113.3 million recognised

evidence.title: Regained Full Ownership of Cazenove Capital from Lloyds JV
evidence.summary: Schroders restructured its Wealth Management business by regaining full ownership of Cazenove Capital in exchange for its stake in Schroders Personal Wealth (SPW), a joint venture with Lloyds Banking Group. This was paired with new multi-year asset management agreements to manage SPW and Scottish Widows assets.
evidence.quote: We have also taken steps to reshape our Wealth Management business, regaining full ownership of Cazenove Capital in exchange for our stake in Schroders Personal Wealth (SPW).

evidence.title: Renewed Multi-Year Asset Management Agreements with Lloyds
evidence.summary: Following the Cazenove/SPW transaction, Schroders renewed its strategic relationship with Lloyds Banking Group through new multi-year asset management agreements to manage SPW and Scottish Widows assets.
evidence.quote: We have renewed our strategic relationship with Lloyds Banking Group by entering into new, multi-year asset management agreements to manage the SPW and Scottish Widows assets.

initiatives.name: Operational Emissions Reduction Programme
initiatives.summary: Schroders has reduced its operational Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 41% from the 2019 base year, driven by office consolidation and energy efficiency projects, as part of its science-based target to reduce emissions by 46% by 2030.

evidence.title: 41% Reduction in Scope 1&2 Emissions vs 2019 Baseline
evidence.summary: Schroders has reduced its operational Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 41% from the 2019 base year, driven by office consolidation and energy efficiency projects, as part of its science-based target to reduce emissions by 46% by 2030.
evidence.quote: Our total operational Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions decreased by 41% from the 2019 base year.

evidence.title: 100% Renewable Electricity Achieved Ahead of Schedule
evidence.summary: Schroders achieved 100% renewable electricity sourcing for its global offices in 2024, one year ahead of its 2025 target, and maintained this in 2025, as part of its RE100 commitment.
evidence.quote: We maintained our target of sourcing 100% renewable electricity for our global offices, which we achieved a year ahead of schedule in 2024.

initiatives.name: Long-Term Asset Funds (LTAF) Distribution Partnerships
initiatives.summary: Schroders partnered with Hargreaves Lansdown, the UK's largest retail investment platform, to offer Long-Term Asset Funds (LTAFs) to a wider group of private investors, broadening retail access to private markets.

evidence.title: Mercer LTAF Mandate in UK Defined Contribution Pensions
evidence.summary: Schroders won a mandate from Mercer in the UK defined contribution pension market, jointly designing a bespoke Long-Term Asset Fund (LTAF) to broaden access to private markets, with Future Growth Capital appointed as investment manager.
evidence.quote: In December 2025, we won a mandate from Mercer in the UK defined contribution pension market, creating a further opportunity to expand our evergreen private markets range. This included the launch of a bespoke long-term asset fund (LTAF), jointly designed with Mercer, broadening access to diversified private markets exposure.

evidence.title: Hargreaves Lansdown LTAF Partnership for Retail Investors
evidence.summary: Schroders partnered with Hargreaves Lansdown, the UK's largest retail investment platform, to offer Long-Term Asset Funds (LTAFs) to a wider group of private investors, broadening retail access to private markets.
evidence.quote: In the UK, we partnered with Hargreaves Lansdown, the UK's largest retail investment platform, to offer two Long-Term Asset Funds (LTAFs) to a wider group of private investors.

initiatives.name: Portfolio Rationalization & Market Exits
initiatives.summary: Schroders rationalised its product offering by merging or closing underperforming strategies while launching new ones, as part of simplifying the client proposition. Over 16% of the Public Markets fund range was identified for merger or closure.

evidence.title: Product Range Rationalisation - Merging/Closing Strategies
evidence.summary: Schroders rationalised its product offering by merging or closing underperforming strategies while launching new ones, as part of simplifying the client proposition. Over 16% of the Public Markets fund range was identified for merger or closure.
evidence.quote: Identified 16.2% of our public fund range to be merged or closed

evidence.title: Market Exits: Brazil, Indonesia, Australia Private Credit, South Korea
evidence.summary: As part of portfolio restructuring, Schroders exited or announced intentions to exit several markets where it lacked scale or strategic advantage, including closing its Munich real estate business, exiting Australian private credit, announcing closure of Brazil operations, progressing South Korea restructuring, and initiating sale of its Indonesian asset management business.
evidence.quote: During the year, we closed our convertibles desk, exited our real estate business in Munich and our private credit business in Australia, announced our intention to close our business in Brazil, and progressed the restructuring of our business in South Korea. In addition, we initiated the sale of our Indonesian asset management business (subject to regulatory approval)

evidence.quote: A new head of Client Group, with supporting appointments, joined in 2025 and has energised our global sales operations. And our new Wealth Management CEO is refreshing his leadership team

initiatives.summary: Schroders maintains its 2021 commitment to transition its business and managed portfolios toward net zero, with science-based targets including aligning in-scope investment portfolios with a 2.2°C pathway by 2030 and 1.5°C pathway by 2040.

evidence.quote: Therefore, in 2021 we made our initial commitment to transitioning our business and the portfolios we manage toward a net zero future. Our commitment remains unchanged.
